title: stakes.wtf: stake a token for gov tokens, grow their value with bribes, unstake into linear vesting
summary: Stake a token into a pool and get gov tokens; bribes sent to the pool raise what each gov token is worth; unstaking burns them and releases tokens linearly over 20 days.
what: stakes.wtf turns any SPL token into a staking pool without new reward tokens. Anyone can open a pool for a mint (2 SOL fee). Stakers deposit the token and get the pool's **gov token** at the current gov price. Anyone can **bribe** the pool by simply sending tokens to its vault; `sync_bribes` credits a share of those extra tokens to the pool each day, which lowers the gov price, so each gov token is now worth more of the underlying token. Unstaking burns all your gov tokens and moves what they're worth into a vesting position that unlocks in 20 equal daily parts. Two ideas are worth learning: value accrual through an exchange rate instead of reward payouts, and vesting as a separate escrow account.
app_note: The fork's own React + Vite app with this devnet program ID and hash routing (`#/vesting`, `#/create`) for static hosting. The program is built with the crate's own `testing` feature, so **one program "day" is one second**, and with the pool-creation fee receiver constant set to our deployer. The only pool uses a test token (5AWQ…cvUb) that only our deployer can mint, so you need some of it to stake. Script: [tests/devnet/patches/stakes-main.py](https://github.com/Blockchains/sol-college/blob/main/tests/devnet/patches/stakes-main.py).

try_steps.see: A `stake` transaction; Your Stake shows 100 and your wallet now holds 100 gov tokens.
ran: Pool row 5AWQ…cvUb, Stake tab, 100, Stake; the row then showed Your Stake 100

try_steps.see: A plain SPL token transfer into the pool vault. TVL doesn't change: the bribe only counts once someone calls `sync_bribes`, which the app never does.
ran: Bribe tab, 20, Bribe; APR then read 2 190

try_steps.see: An `unstake` transaction: your gov tokens are burned and a vesting position appears on the **Vesting** page with Claim Per Day = amount / 20.
ran: Claim tab, Unstake; the Vesting page then listed the position at 5 per day

try_steps.see: A `claim_vested` transaction. In this testing build a day is a second, so after 20 s the full amount is released and the position closes.
ran: Vesting page, Claim; the position closed and the wallet held 480 (500 − 100 − 20 + 100)

instructions.name: `initialize_pool`: pool, vault, gov mint, fee

refs.note: constants; the deployment sets FEE_RECEIVER_PUBKEY to our deployer and builds with `testing`

steps: One pool per mint: seeds `["staking_pool", mint]`; a second pool for the same mint fails (account already in use, in Proof).

The vault is a token account at a PDA whose **authority is the pool PDA**, and the gov mint's mint authority is also the pool. Only the program, signing with the pool's seeds, can move staked tokens or mint gov.
`fee_receiver` must equal `FEE_RECEIVER_PUBKEY` (`InvalidFeeReceiver`, in Proof) and gets 2 SOL by System Program CPI.
`SECONDS_PER_DAY` is 1 under the `testing` feature; this deployment uses it.

instructions.name: `stake`: tokens in, gov out
steps: `has_one = gov_mint` rejects a different gov mint (`InvalidMint`, in Proof).
The user's tokens go into the vault (the user signs); then the pool signs a `mint_to` with `new_with_signer(&[pool seeds])`.
gov minted = amount × `gov_price` / 10⁹. Gov price starts at 10⁹ (1 gov per token): B staked 100 and got 100 gov.

instructions.name: `sync_bribes`: turn bribes into value
steps: Unsynced bribes = vault balance − `active_balance`. Each day passed releases 5% of them (`BRIBE_SHARE_PER_DAY = 50` ‰), at least 0.1% of the vault, capped at all of them.
The released amount is added to `active_balance`, and `gov_price = gov_supply × 10⁹ / active_balance`.
In our script the pool was old enough (in one-second days) that all 50 bribed tokens were released at once: active 150, gov price 666,666,666. B's 100 gov were now worth 150 tokens.

instructions.name: `unstake`: burn and start vesting
steps: Converts **all** your gov tokens: amount = gov × 10⁹ / gov_price (100 × 10⁹ / 666,666,666 = 150). There's no partial unstake.
The pool signs a transfer of that amount from the staking vault to a new vesting vault, records `claim_per_day = amount / 20` (7.5 for B), then burns your gov tokens.

instructions.name: `claim_vested`: linear unlock
steps: `has_one = owner`: only the position's owner can claim (`InvalidOwner` when A tried B's, in Proof).
Pays `days_passed × claim_per_day`; if what would remain is less than one more day's share, pays everything and closes both accounts, returning their rent.
B's first claim paid 82.5 = 11 × 7.5 (11 one-second days had passed by the time it landed); the second paid the remaining 67.5 and closed the position. B ended with 1,050 tokens from 1,000.

innovation.title: rewards as an exchange rate, and the pool PDA as the only authority
innovation.text: Nobody is ever paid a reward directly. Bribes raise the pool's token balance, `sync_bribes` folds them in, and the gov price falls, so each gov token redeems for more. One pool PDA is the authority of the staking vault, every vesting vault and the gov mint, and signs for all of them with `["staking_pool", mint, bump]`.
more: Because stake and unstake use the gov price as stored, the order of calls matters. `stake` doesn't sync first, so whoever stakes just before a `sync_bribes` shares bribes that arrived before they joined. `unstake` doesn't sync either, so bribes not yet synced stay behind for the remaining stakers (Exercises 2 and 3).

frontend.title: Same PDAs in the browser
steps: Pool from the mint, vault from the pool, vesting vault from the position, exactly the program's seeds.

frontend.title: Instruction builders
steps: Unstake generates a fresh keypair for the vesting position, which must co-sign; the vesting vault is derived from it.
Bribe isn't a program instruction at all, just `createTransferInstruction` into the vault.

frontend.title: Create Pool is out of date
steps: No `feeReceiver` in the accounts: the app's IDL predates it, so the next account (the System Program) lands in that slot and the program rejects it with `AccountNotSystemOwned` (0xbc3).

frontend.title: Sending: extra signers, then the wallet
steps: Adds a priority fee, signs with the generated keypairs, asks the wallet to sign, then sends the raw transaction and confirms it.

frontend.title: The APR column
steps: APR = (vault ÷ active balance) ÷ 20 × 365 × 100. With 100 staked and 20 bribed: 1.2 ÷ 20 × 36,500 = 2,190, the number the app showed after our UI bribe.

exercises.title: Follow the exchange rate
steps: From Proof: B stakes 100, A bribes 50, `sync_bribes`.
Compute the new gov price and what B's 100 gov redeem for.
exercises.hint: The exchange rate is a ratio of two on-chain balances (pool tokens vs gov-token supply), not a price oracle.
exercises.approach: Read both balances before and after the recorded bribe, compute the rate with the program's formula, and compare to what a small stake would mint. It should match the recorded stake transaction.

exercises.title: Join right before a sync
steps: In a local test: stake 100 (B), bribe 100, wait several "days", then have C stake 100 and only then call `sync_bribes`.
Unstake both.
exercises.expect: C gets part of a bribe that arrived before C staked, because `stake` uses the stale gov price. Fix: call the bribe sync logic at the start of `stake` and `unstake`.
exercises.hint: Joining immediately before a `sync` (a bribe or a harvest) can give you a share of a bribe you didn't wait for — or lock you out, depending on the order of updates.
exercises.approach: On a local validator, stake in the same transaction slot as a bribe (or immediately before `sync`) and compare the gov tokens minted with staking immediately after. The difference is the 'join right before a sync' effect the lesson points at; describe it from the numbers, don't invent them.

exercises.title: Where did the UI bribe go?
steps: Our UI wallet staked 100, bribed 20 and unstaked; read its balance in Try-it step 5 (480 = 500 − 100 − 20 + 100).
exercises.expect: It got back exactly its 100: the 20 was never synced, and with `active_balance` at 0 `get_current_bribe_amount` returns 0. The 20 stays in the vault for whoever stakes next and syncs.
exercises.hint: Follow the bribe transaction on Explorer: the token destination is an account. Compare it to the pool's vault.
exercises.approach: If the destination is a different ATA (a fee account, or the user's own), that is why the UI bribe didn't raise the rate. Point at the client code that picked the account, and at the recorded signature.

exercises.title: Fix the APR
steps: Change Pool.tsx line 121 to use `(vault.amount - activeBalance) / activeBalance`.
exercises.expect: With 100 staked and 20 bribed it shows 365 instead of 2,190; with no bribes it shows 0 instead of 1,825.
exercises.hint: APR in the UI is often a display-only calculation. If it uses the wrong period or ignores the scale, it will not match a one-day vest.
exercises.approach: Recompute APR from the on-chain rate and the vest duration, and fix the display to that formula. It should then be consistent with exercise 1's withdrawable amount.

exercises.title: Repair Create Pool
steps: Regenerate the app's IDL from the program (`anchor build`) or add `feeReceiver` to `createCreatePoolInstruction`, set to the fee receiver constant.
exercises.expect: Create Pool sends an `initialize_pool` that moves 2 SOL to the fee receiver and creates the pool, as our script did (2yVByakS…).
exercises.hint: Create Pool may fail because of a missing account, a wrong PDA, or an ATA that hasn't been created. The error in the logs is the starting point.
exercises.approach: Reproduce the failure locally, read the program logs, and add the missing account (or the missing `init`) so Create Pool succeeds. Don't change the pool's economics, only the accounts the instruction expects.

not_covered: Stake, bribe, unstake and vesting claim were clicked through in the app. Create Pool can't work in the app (out-of-date IDL), so the pool was created by script, and sync_bribes, which the app never calls, was only run by script. This is the testing build (1 day = 1 second), so vesting finishes in seconds. Only holders of the test token 5AWQ… can stake in the existing pool.
objectives: Stake a token, receive gov tokens, and watch an exchange rate move when a bribe is added to the pool.
Unstake into a linear vest, and compute how much is withdrawable at a given time.
Find why a UI bribe didn't land where the label said, and repair a Create Pool path that fails.
prereqs: Phantom on devnet, plus whatever test token the app mints for you.
[Colosseum](/lessons/colosseum/) (staking, time) and [gree](/lessons/gree/) (token CPIs). This is the densest token-economics lesson.
